findings._why: The dedup table, its payload_hash conflict detection, and the SAVEPOINT-free race handling all exist to make a replayed event_id a no-op, but no production caller can ever replay an event_id: every call site generates a brand new uuid4. So the retry the design is built for happens anyway. A designer double-clicks 'pass', or the client retries after a lost response, and pass_check — which unlike record_actual_data and confirm_actual_data has no state precondition at all — runs a second time and emits a second actual_data_replaces_design under a new id. The table also grows by one never-reusable row per emit, forever.

findings._why: The new PUT /api/v1/equipment/{id}/actual-data and POST .../actual-data/confirm return 422 envelopes whose `code` is `ACTUAL_DATA_VALIDATION` or `DEVIATION_BLOCKS_CONFIRMATION` (the test suite at tests/api/v1/test_supplier_actual_data_api.py:156 asserts the former is emitted). _source_map.key: security|pcs-backend/app/api/v1/supplier.py|210|[a01/cwe-841] `pass_check`/`reject_check` enforce no state precondition — a reviewer can mark never-entered equipment confirmed and bypass the entire designer-submit + deviation gate
correctness|pcs-backend/app/services/supplier/confirmation_service.py|98|pass_check has no state precondition — a checker can mark equipment confirmed without ever passing the deviation gate

findings._why: The four-eyes control this router exists to enforce is bypassable by any user holding the REVIEWER role alone. `check_actual_data` loads the equipment and calls `pass_check_svc` unconditionally; `pass_check` writes `actual_data_status = CONFIRMED` and flushes with no check on the current status. A REVIEWER who has project access can therefore drive an equipment from `NOT_ENTERED` (no designer ever typed a single value, no deviation report ever generated, no designer ever submitted) straight to `CONFIRMED`, and the router returns 200 with `actual_data_status: "CONFIRMED"`. The downstream effect is not cosmetic: `pass_check` fires the `actual_data_replaces_design` event with `before=equipment.design_parameters_json` and `after=equipment.actual_data_json` — for a never-entered machine `after` is `None` — and the confirmation gate (`can_confirm`, the whole fail-closed deviation engine of S4-2) lives only in `confirm_actual_data`, which this path never reaches. The resulting `CONFIRMED` status is exactly what `record_actual_data` treats as the lock that forbids re-entry (`ACTUAL_DATA_LOCKED`), so the equipment is permanently frozen against the designer who was supposed to fill it in. `reject_check` has the mirror-image gap: it resets a `CONFIRMED` record to `PENDING_CONFIRM` with no precondition, which unlocks the re-entry channel on any record. The fix is the repo's own guard pattern applied at the service boundary — raise `PcsError(409/422, ...)` when `equipment.actual_data_status` is not `PENDING_CONFIRM` before either transition, mirroring how `record_actual_data` already gates on `CONFIRMED`.

findings.suggested_fix:
Add a precondition and a re-gate at the top of `pass_check`, mirroring the shape already used by `confirm_actual_data` (same module, same `_error` helper):

```python
if equipment.actual_data_status != ActualDataStatus.PENDING_CONFIRM.value:
    raise _error(
        "ACTUAL_DATA_NOT_SUBMITTED",
        f"实际数据当前为 {equipment.actual_data_status} —— 校核通过前须由设计人先提交确认",
        status=409,
    )

report = build_report(equipment)
if not can_confirm(report):
    raise _error(
        "DEVIATION_BLOCKS_CONFIRMATION",
        f"存在不合格或不可判项，禁止校核通过：{report.blocking_reason}",
    )
```

_source_map.key: security|pcs-backend/app/services/supplier/deviation_report.py|208|[a03/cwe-1236] excel export writes the designer-controlled parameter name into a live formula cell — verified data_type 'f'

findings._why: `ActualDataEntry.name` is an arbitrary string from the designer's PUT body (`Field(min_length=1, max_length=100)`, no character restriction). `build_report` iterates `for name in actual:` and every row's `parameter` field carries that string verbatim into the workbook. openpyxl does not escape a leading `=`, so the cell is persisted as a live formula. I confirmed this end to end: with `name = "=cmd|'/c calc'!A0"` the exported workbook round-trips as `B2 "=cmd|'/c calc'!A0" f` — `f` is openpyxl's formula data type. The attacker is any DESIGNER or PROCESS_CONTROLLER on the project (the export is VIEWER-gated, so the file reaches every viewer and any downstream recipient of the export); the victim is whoever opens the file in Excel, where the formula evaluates. On older Excel that is DDE / command execution; on current Excel the reliable payload is `=HYPERLINK(...)` or an external-cell-reference exfiltration of the workbook's own contents. Because the write role and the read role are different people here, this is a stored, cross-role delivery mechanism: a designer plants it, a viewer or process engineer trips it. The same unescaped value also reaches `unit` (column E) and, via `tag_number`, column A.

Make the destructive case explicit and gated, and make the seed script's dry-run the default. In `apply_design_parameters`:

async def apply_design_parameters(
    session: AsyncSession,
    project_id: uuid.UUID,
    *,
    overwrite: bool = False,
    dry_run: bool = False,
) -> int:
    ...

            skipped.append(record.tag_number)

FROM equipment_list
WHERE design_parameters_json IS NOT NULL;

FROM equipment_list
WHERE project_id = '<PROJECT_ID>' AND design_parameters_json IS NOT NULL;

_source_map.key: api-contract|pcs-backend/app/schemas/supplier.py|22|unbounded free-form parameter names on a public write surface whose read surface is a closed rule set -- nothing in the contract tells a client which keys are judgeable

findings._why: The write side accepts any 1-100 character string as a parameter name and stores it verbatim as a key of the public `actual_data_json` object; the read side interprets those keys against a closed, fixed rule set and returns `UNVERDICTABLE` for every key it does not recognise. Nothing in the request schema, the response schema, or the endpoint docs states the set of meaningful keys, so a client can successfully write data that is permanently unjudgeable -- the write returns 200 with the offending value echoed back, and the failure only surfaces later as a `UNVERDICTABLE` row and `can_confirm: false`. Because the endpoint docstring at supplier.py:153-154 already records that `design_parameters_json` has no writer (so production reports are entirely `UNVERDICTABLE` and `can_confirm` is effectively always false), the write surface currently has no path to a judged report at all. Compounding this, the response type is a bare `dict`, which the generator emits as `{[key: string]: unknown} | null` -- the client gets no per-value typing and must re-narrow `unknown` itself.
evidence: pcs-backend/app/schemas/supplier.py:22 -- `name: str = Field(min_length=1, max_length=100, description="参数名")` -- any string is a legal key; there is no allow-list, no enum, and no cross-reference to the engine's rule set.

_source_map.key: security|pcs-backend/app/schemas/supplier.py|23|[a03/cwe-20] the strict-float contract on `actualdataentry.value` is enforced only by pydantic's lax coercion, so the service's own string/bool rejection is unreachable dead code on the api path

findings._why: Both the schema docstring ("value 严格数值 —— 字符串数字在 UI 上是录入错误, 不是可容忍的输入") and `actual_data_service._coerce_value` (docstring: "不接受 '100' 这类字符串数字", with an explicit `isinstance(raw, bool)` rejection) state that string numerics and booleans must be refused. Neither guard actually fires on the router path, because Pydantic v2 runs first in lax mode and hands the service an already-coerced `float`. Verified against the real schema: `'100' -> 100.0`, `True -> 1.0`, `'NaN' -> nan`, `'Infinity' -> inf`. So the service's boolean branch is unreachable from `PUT /actual-data` and the string-digit rule is not enforced at all. The security-relevant edge is that non-finite floats survive validation: `float('nan')` reaches `deviation_service.evaluate`, where every comparison against NaN is false, so the `ASYMMETRIC_BAND` rule falls through to `return Evaluation(QUALIFIED, deviation)` — I verified `can_confirm` returns `True` for a pump whose entire actual-data set is `{"扬程": {"value": NaN}}`, i.e. a value that was never measured would clear the SPEC §3.2.4(4) confirmation gate. That specific bypass does not reach production today: PostgreSQL 18.6 rejects `NaN` as a JSONB literal (`InvalidTextRepresentationError` on `select 'NaN'::jsonb`), so the write fails with a 500 rather than persisting — the practical impact today is an unhandled 500 on a request a client can trigger, not a confirmed forged value. I file it at P2 and 75 for that reason: the validation contract the code documents is not the contract the code enforces, and the moment a non-finite value becomes storable — or a numeric-typed column replaces the JSONB — the NaN-to-QUALIFIED path becomes live.
evidence: pcs-backend/app/schemas/supplier.py:23 — `    value: float = Field(description="实测值 (可为负, 如冬季设计温度)")` — a bare `float` with no `Field(strict=True)` and no `allow_inf_nan=False`.

Executed against the real `ActualDataEntry` model: `'100' -> 100.0`, `True -> 1.0`, `'NaN' -> nan`, `'Infinity' -> inf`, `None REJECT ValidationError`. Pydantic lax mode coerces the exact inputs that `actual_data_service.py:33-39` `_coerce_value` exists to reject.

pcs-backend/app/services/supplier/actual_data_service.py:35 — `    if isinstance(raw, bool) or not isinstance(raw, (int, float)):` — unreachable from the router, because `model_dump()` at `supplier.py:121` yields `value` as an already-coerced `float`.

pcs-backend/app/services/supplier/deviation_service.py:249 — `        return Evaluation(QUALIFIED, deviation)` is the fall-through of `ASYMMETRIC_BAND`; with `deviation = nan` both guards at lines 245 and 247 compare false, so execution lands here. Executed: `扬程 QUALIFIED nan` and `can_confirm = True` for `actual_data_json={'扬程':{'value':float('nan'),...}}` against a design value of 2100.0.

The persistence leg was checked against the live database and does not hold: `PostgreSQL 18.6`, `jsonb NaN ERR: asyncpg.exceptions.InvalidTextRepresentationError`. This is why severity is P2 rather than P0 — the gate bypass is demonstrable in-process but not yet reachable through stored data.
findings.first_evidence: pcs-backend/app/schemas/supplier.py:23 — `    value: float = Field(description="实测值 (可为负, 如冬季设计温度)")`
findings.suggested_fix:
Make the schema enforce the contract it documents, so the service-level checks become defence in depth rather than the only (unreachable) defence:

```python
value: float = Field(
    description="实测值 (可为负, 如冬季设计温度)",
    strict=True,
    allow_inf_nan=False,
)
```

`strict=True` rejects `'100'` and `True` at the boundary, matching both docstrings; `allow_inf_nan=False` closes the NaN/Infinity path into `evaluate` regardless of storage format. This is a breaking change for any client currently sending string numerics, which is precisely the behaviour the two docstrings say should not be tolerated — worth confirming against the frontend types (`pcs-frontend/src/types/api.d.ts` is in this diff) before applying. Assumption: no legitimate caller depends on lax numeric coercion; if one does, the fix is to fix that caller, not to widen the field.
findings.title: [A03/CWE-20] The strict-float contract on `ActualDataEntry.value` is enforced only by Pydantic's lax coercion, so the service's own string/bool rejection is unreachable dead code on the API path

findings._why: The generator emits `design_value: number | string | null` into the frontend's TypeScript types, so a client that formats or does arithmetic on the design value (the obvious use in a deviation report -- percent difference against `actual_value`) compiles cleanly and then throws at runtime on the string case.
